def: A tag on a technical claim saying what kind of claim it is: verified (cited source), derived (reasoned from verified facts), synthetic example, implementation-dependent, version-dependent, or unknown.

The ranking used when sources disagree: official NVM Express specifications, then PCI-SIG specifications, Linux kernel documentation/source, device vendor documentation, analyzer vendor documentation, peer-reviewed papers, books, and community material last. Check first whether the sources answer the same question.

A header recording document, revision, ratification date, status, older versions that may differ, and where and when the source was checked, placed at the start of any specification-level lesson or report.

A block attached to a specification-sensitive statement listing the official document, revision, topic, date verified, what the source establishes and what it does not establish. Cites section titles, never unverified section numbers.
The phrase used when a field or event needed for a conclusion is not present in a capture (filtered, not exported, not decoded). It names the missing evidence instead of guessing.
The statement that follows an analogy: what maps well, what does not map, and what engineering detail the analogy hides.
A record kept while analysing an NVMe queue: queue ID, size, head, tail, CIDs, phase, memory location, ownership, producer and consumer, with the evidence for each and the evidence that is missing.

The twelve stages a concept passes through to be mastered: intuition, terminology, structure, mechanism, example, counterexample, trace, lab, failure, recovery, explanation by the learner, assessment.
What is it, why does it exist, how does it work, what happens if it fails, and how would you prove what happened. A concept is not mastered until all five can be answered with named evidence.
Mistaking a concept at one layer for a neighbouring one, such as an NVMe CQE for a PCIe Completion TLP, a doorbell for a command, or an NVMe revision for a PCIe generation.

A uniform record for any observation: event ID, timestamp, source, destination, layer, protocol, type, direction, address, tag/CID, payload, status, expected next, actual next, correlation ID, evidence and confidence.
Arranging events into slots T0 (system state) to T7 (software notification) for the expected and the observed behaviour, then comparing them to find the first deviation.

Using the absence of an event as evidence. Valid only if the event was expected and the capture is known to be complete enough to have observed it; otherwise say it is not visible in the captured interval.
What a capture could have observed: start and end, completeness of timestamps, filters, decode omissions, and whether both directions were captured. Bounds every claim about absence.
A trace invented for teaching or test design, labelled 'synthetic teaching trace, not a real device capture'. It can illustrate a mechanism but is never evidence about a device.

Deterministic conversion of a raw capture into a normalized event schema, transaction groups, a timeline and anomalies, with region-relative addresses, symbolic tags and one clock. Done before any automated or LLM reasoning.
Comparing a known-good (golden) trace with a suspect trace after normalization, aligning initialization, commands, queues, TLPs, completions and interrupts, to find the first divergence.
The earliest aligned event at which a suspect trace differs from the golden trace. It is where investigation starts, not automatically the root cause.

A breakdown of end-to-end I/O latency into components (application, driver, queue, PCIe, controller, media, completion, interrupt) used to find the dominant term and predict the effect of changing one component.

The coding of data bits into transmitted symbols on a PCIe lane: 8b/10b for Gen1 and Gen2, 128b/130b for Gen3 to Gen5; Gen6 Flit mode uses fixed-size flits with FEC and CRC. Reduces payload bandwidth below the raw signalling rate.
